# The First Dream

In the time before time, when the world was young and formless, there lived a weaver named Somnia who worked endlessly at her loom. Day and night, she wove the fabric of reality—mountains and rivers, forests and deserts—but her creations were cold and still.

One evening, exhausted from her labors, Somnia fell asleep at her loom. As she slumbered, something miraculous occurred: threads of starlight began weaving themselves into patterns she had never imagined. They formed impossible cities, flying creatures, and oceans that floated in the sky. When she awakened, these visions vanished like morning mist.

Somnia wept, for she had glimpsed a beauty beyond her skill. But then she understood—what she had witnessed was the first dream, born from the space between waking and sleeping.

From that day forward, Somnia changed her purpose. By day, she wove the solid world as before. But by night, she would rest, and in resting, she would dream. These dreams she gathered like gossamer thread and wove into the minds of all living things yet to come.

This is why we dream: we carry within us fragments of Somnia's visions, reminders that reality is not all there is.
